title: A sticky situation: why Singapore still won't sell you chewing gum

words.zh: 棘手的局面、尴尬的处境
words.note: sticky 本义“黏的”，引申为“棘手的、难办的”：a sticky problem（棘手的问题）。
words.ctx: A sticky situation: why Singapore still won't sell you chewing gum

ex.en: Forgetting her name put me in a [[sticky situation]].
ex.zh: 忘了她的名字让我很尴尬。

ex.en: He talked his way out of a [[sticky situation]].
ex.zh: 他靠一张嘴摆脱了困境。

words.def: a difficult or embarrassing situation

cloze.before: A
cloze.after: situation: why Singapore still won't sell you chewing gum
cloze.szh: 棘手的局面：新加坡为什么至今还不卖口香糖给你

words.note: 一个城市就是一个国家：Singapore and Monaco are city-states. 古希腊的雅典也是城邦（city-state）。
words.ctx: More than three decades after it banned the stuff, the city-state shows little sign of relenting.

ex.en: Singapore is a small but wealthy [[city-state]].
ex.zh: 新加坡是个小而富裕的城市国家。

ex.en: Ancient Athens was a powerful [[city-state]].
ex.zh: 古代雅典是一个强大的城邦。

words.def: a city that is also an independent country

cloze.before: More than three decades after it banned the stuff, the
cloze.after: shows little sign of relenting.
cloze.szh: 禁止这东西三十多年后，这个城市国家仍然丝毫没有松口的迹象。

words.note: show no / little sign of doing sth：The rain showed no sign of stopping.（雨丝毫没有要停的意思。）
words.ctx: More than three decades after it banned the stuff, the city-state shows little sign of relenting.

ex.en: The rain [[showed no sign of]] stopping.
ex.zh: 雨丝毫没有要停的意思。

ex.en: Prices [[show little sign of]] falling.
ex.zh: 价格几乎没有下降的迹象。

words.def: to seem very unlikely to do something

cloze.before: More than three decades after it banned the stuff, the city-state shows little
cloze.after: of relenting.
cloze.hint: 几乎没有……的迹象（shows little ___ of）
cloze.szh: 禁止这东西三十多年后，这个城市国家仍然丝毫没有松口的迹象。

words.note: 原本坚持的态度软化：Her parents finally relented.（她父母最终让步了。）形容词 relentless（毫不留情的）。
words.ctx: More than three decades after it banned the stuff, the city-state shows little sign of relenting.

ex.en: Her parents finally [[relented]] and let her go.
ex.zh: 她父母最终松口，让她去了。

ex.en: The storm showed no sign of [[relenting]].
ex.zh: 暴风雨丝毫没有减弱的迹象。

words.def: to finally agree to something after refusing; (of bad weather) to become less strong

cf.diff: give in 是普通的“屈服、让步”；relent 更书面，指之前很强硬的人终于“心软、松口”。

cloze.before: More than three decades after it banned the stuff, the city-state shows little sign of
cloze.szh: 禁止这东西三十多年后，这个城市国家仍然丝毫没有松口的迹象。

words.zh: 令人费解的、莫名其妙的
words.note: baffle（使困惑）+ -ing。I find it baffling that ...（我搞不懂为什么……）
words.ctx: Visitors find the rule baffling; many locals barely notice it.

ex.en: The instructions were completely [[baffling]].
ex.zh: 说明书完全看不懂。

ex.en: Doctors were [[baffled]] by her illness.
ex.zh: 医生们对她的病情感到困惑。

words.def: impossible to understand or explain

cf.diff: confusing 是“让人搞不清楚”；baffling 语气更强，指“完全想不通、莫名其妙”。

ex.en: The instructions are really [[confusing]].
ex.zh: 说明书写得很让人糊涂。

cloze.before: Visitors find the rule
cloze.after: ; many locals barely notice it.
cloze.szh: 游客觉得这条规定莫名其妙；很多本地人却几乎注意不到它。

words.note: 挑起眉毛表示惊讶或不赞同：His decision raised a few eyebrows.（他的决定让一些人很惊讶。）
words.ctx: In 1992 Singapore made it illegal to import or sell chewing gum, a law that still raises eyebrows abroad.

ex.en: Her bright green hair [[raised eyebrows]] at the office.
ex.zh: 她那头亮绿色的头发在办公室引人侧目。

ex.en: The price [[raised a few eyebrows]].
ex.zh: 这个价格让一些人吃了一惊。

words.def: to make people surprised or slightly shocked

cloze.before: In 1992 Singapore made it illegal to import or sell chewing gum, a law that still
cloze.after: eyebrows abroad.
cloze.szh: 1992 年，新加坡规定进口或销售口香糖都是违法的，这条法律至今仍让外国人惊讶。

words.note: the reasoning behind a decision（某个决定背后的理由）。动词 reason（推理）。
words.ctx: The government's reasoning was practical rather than moral.

ex.en: I don't understand the [[reasoning]] behind this rule.
ex.zh: 我不明白这条规定背后的道理。

ex.en: Her [[reasoning]] was simple: it's too expensive.
ex.zh: 她的理由很简单：太贵了。

words.def: the process of thinking about something in a logical way; the reasons behind an opinion

cloze.before: The government's
cloze.after: was practical rather than moral.
cloze.szh: 政府的理由是出于实际，而不是出于道德。

words.note: fortune 是“财富、一大笔钱”。cost a fortune（贵得要命），make a fortune（发大财）。
words.ctx: Cleaners were spending a fortune scraping gum off pavements, stairwells and lift buttons.

ex.en: They [[spent a fortune]] on the wedding.
ex.zh: 他们在婚礼上花了一大笔钱。

ex.en: That coat must have [[cost a fortune]].
ex.zh: 那件外套一定贵得要命。

words.def: to spend a very large amount of money

cloze.before: Cleaners were spending a
cloze.after: scraping gum off pavements, stairwells and lift buttons.
cloze.szh: 清洁工花了大笔钱，从人行道、楼梯间和电梯按钮上刮口香糖。

words.note: scrape A off B：scrape ice off the windscreen（把挡风玻璃上的冰刮掉）。也说 scrape off sth。
words.ctx: Cleaners were spending a fortune scraping gum off pavements, stairwells and lift buttons.

ex.en: He [[scraped off]] the old paint.
ex.zh: 他把旧漆刮掉了。

ex.en: I spent ten minutes [[scraping off]] the ice.
ex.zh: 我花了十分钟把冰刮掉。

words.def: to remove something from a surface by rubbing it with something sharp or hard

cloze.before: Cleaners were spending a fortune
cloze.after: gum off pavements, stairwells and lift buttons.
cloze.szh: 清洁工花了大笔钱，从人行道、楼梯间和电梯按钮上刮口香糖。

words.note: 楼里装楼梯的竖井空间。staircase 是楼梯本身。
words.ctx: Cleaners were spending a fortune scraping gum off pavements, stairwells and lift buttons.

ex.en: The kids played in the [[stairwell]].
ex.zh: 孩子们在楼梯间里玩。

ex.en: The [[stairwell]] was dark and cold.
ex.zh: 楼梯间又黑又冷。

words.def: the space in a building that contains the stairs

cloze.before: Cleaners were spending a fortune scraping gum off pavements,
cloze.after: and lift buttons.
cloze.szh: 清洁工花了大笔钱，从人行道、楼梯间和电梯按钮上刮口香糖。

words.zh: 压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草、忍无可忍
words.note: 来自谚语 the straw that broke the camel's back。That's the last straw!（我受够了！）
words.ctx: The last straw, according to most accounts, came when vandals stuck gum on the door sensors of the new metro trains, causing doors to jam and services to stall.

ex.en: Being late again was [[the last straw]].
ex.zh: 又迟到，这让人忍无可忍了。

ex.en: When the TV broke, that was [[the last straw]].
ex.zh: 电视坏了，这成了压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草。

words.def: the last in a series of bad things that makes you finally lose patience

cloze.before: The last
cloze.after: , according to most accounts, came when vandals stuck gum on the door sensors of the new metro trains, causing doors to jam and services to stall.
cloze.szh: 据大多数说法，压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草，是有人搞破坏，把口香糖粘在新地铁列车的车门感应器上，导致车门卡住、列车停运。

words.note: account 在这里是“叙述、说法”。by all accounts：大家都说。
words.ctx: The last straw, according to most accounts, came when vandals stuck gum on the door sensors of the new metro trains, causing doors to jam and services to stall.

ex.en: [[By all accounts]], she is a brilliant teacher.
ex.zh: 大家都说她是个出色的老师。

ex.en: [[According to most accounts]], the fire started in the kitchen.
ex.zh: 据大多数说法，火是从厨房烧起来的。

words.def: according to what most people have said or written about something

cloze.before: The last straw, according to most
cloze.after: , came when vandals stuck gum on the door sensors of the new metro trains, causing doors to jam and services to stall.
cloze.hint: 据大多数说法（according to most ___）
cloze.szh: 据大多数说法，压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草，是有人搞破坏，把口香糖粘在新地铁列车的车门感应器上，导致车门卡住、列车停运。

words.note: 名词“破坏公物的人”。动词是 vandalise（见下一个词），破坏公物的行为叫 vandalism。
words.ctx: The last straw, according to most accounts, came when vandals stuck gum on the door sensors of the new metro trains, causing doors to jam and services to stall.

ex.en: [[Vandals]] smashed the bus shelter.
ex.zh: 有人把公交候车亭砸了。

ex.en: The police caught the [[vandal]] on camera.
ex.zh: 警察通过监控拍到了那个破坏公物的人。

words.def: a person who deliberately damages public property

cloze.before: The last straw, according to most accounts, came when
cloze.after: stuck gum on the door sensors of the new metro trains, causing doors to jam and services to stall.
cloze.szh: 据大多数说法，压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草，是有人搞破坏，把口香糖粘在新地铁列车的车门感应器上，导致车门卡住、列车停运。

words.note: The car stalled.（车熄火了。）The talks stalled.（谈判陷入僵局。）
words.ctx: The last straw, according to most accounts, came when vandals stuck gum on the door sensors of the new metro trains, causing doors to jam and services to stall.

ex.en: The car [[stalled]] at the traffic lights.
ex.zh: 车在红绿灯前熄火了。

ex.en: Peace talks have [[stalled]] again.
ex.zh: 和谈再次陷入僵局。

words.def: (of an engine or vehicle) to stop suddenly; to delay doing something; to stop making progress

cf.diff: stop 是最普通的“停下”，可以是主动、正常地停；stall 是意外地“熄火、停滞”，车或发动机突然停下、谈判或计划卡住不动，常带“出了问题”的意思。

ex.en: The bus [[stopped]] at the lights.
ex.zh: 公交车在红绿灯前停下了。

ex.en: The car [[stalled]] at the lights.
ex.zh: 车在红绿灯前熄火了。

cf.diff: stall 还可以指人“故意拖延时间、敷衍”，这时接近 delay，但 delay 是中性的“推迟”，stall 带“故意拖”的意思。

ex.en: Stop [[stalling]] and give me an answer.
ex.zh: 别拖了，给我个答复。

cf.diff: 车熄火是 stall，重新发动是 start (up)。

ex.en: The engine won't [[start]].
ex.zh: 发动机打不着火。

cloze.before: The last straw, according to most accounts, came when vandals stuck gum on the door sensors of the new metro trains, causing doors to jam and services to
cloze.szh: 据大多数说法，压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草，是有人搞破坏，把口香糖粘在新地铁列车的车门感应器上，导致车门卡住、列车停运。

words.note: pride 作动词只用于这个结构：She prides herself on her cooking.（她对自己的厨艺很自豪。）
words.ctx: Since independence it has prided itself on being clean, green and orderly, and its leaders have never been shy about regulating daily life to keep it that way.

ex.en: The hotel [[prides itself on]] its service.
ex.zh: 这家酒店以服务为傲。

ex.en: She [[prides herself on]] never being late.
ex.zh: 她以从不迟到为荣。

words.def: to be proud of a quality or skill that you have

cf.diff: be proud of 用得最广；pride oneself on 强调“对自己的某种品质或能力引以为豪”，主语通常是自己的特点。

ex.en: I'm so [[proud of]] you.
ex.zh: 我真为你骄傲。

cloze.before: Since independence it has
cloze.after: itself on being clean, green and orderly, and its leaders have never been shy about regulating daily life to keep it that way.
cloze.szh: 独立以来，新加坡一直以干净、绿化好、秩序井然为荣，它的领导人也从不避讳通过规管日常生活来保持这种状态。

words.note: an orderly queue（排得整整齐齐的队），in an orderly way（有条不紊地）。注意 -ly 结尾但它是形容词。
words.ctx: Since independence it has prided itself on being clean, green and orderly, and its leaders have never been shy about regulating daily life to keep it that way.

ex.en: Please leave the building in an [[orderly]] way.
ex.zh: 请有序地离开大楼。

ex.en: Her desk is always neat and [[orderly]].
ex.zh: 她的桌子总是整整齐齐。

words.def: arranged or organized in a neat, tidy way; behaving well

cloze.before: Since independence it has prided itself on being clean, green and
cloze.after: , and its leaders have never been shy about regulating daily life to keep it that way.
cloze.szh: 独立以来，新加坡一直以干净、绿化好、秩序井然为荣，它的领导人也从不避讳通过规管日常生活来保持这种状态。

words.note: 用规则管控：regulate the use of drones（规范无人机的使用）。名词 regulation（规定）。
words.ctx: Since independence it has prided itself on being clean, green and orderly, and its leaders have never been shy about regulating daily life to keep it that way.

ex.en: The government plans to [[regulate]] online games.
ex.zh: 政府计划规范网络游戏。

ex.en: Sweat helps [[regulate]] body temperature.
ex.zh: 出汗有助于调节体温。

words.def: to control an activity or process, usually by rules

cloze.before: Since independence it has prided itself on being clean, green and orderly, and its leaders have never been shy about
cloze.after: daily life to keep it that way.
cloze.szh: 独立以来，新加坡一直以干净、绿化好、秩序井然为荣，它的领导人也从不避讳通过规管日常生活来保持这种状态。

words.note: Long hours are part of the deal.（工作时间长是这份工作的一部分，没办法。）
words.ctx: Fines for littering, spitting and failing to flush public toilets have long been part of the deal.

ex.en: Working weekends is [[part of the deal]].
ex.zh: 周末加班是这份工作的一部分。

ex.en: Crowds are [[part of the deal]] when you visit Paris.
ex.zh: 去巴黎就得接受人多。

words.def: something you must accept as part of an arrangement

cloze.before: Fines for littering, spitting and failing to flush public toilets have long been part of the
cloze.hint: （不得不接受的）一部分（part of the ___）
cloze.szh: 乱扔垃圾、随地吐痰、上完公厕不冲水都会被罚款，这一直是这份“约定”的一部分。

words.zh: 保姆式国家（管得太多的政府）
words.note: 贬义，批评政府什么都管：Critics call the smoking ban an example of the nanny state.
words.ctx: To outsiders, such rules can look like a nanny state at its most fussy.

ex.en: Some people call the new rules the [[nanny state]] gone mad.
ex.zh: 有人说新规定是保姆式国家管疯了。

ex.en: He hates the idea of a [[nanny state]].
ex.zh: 他讨厌政府什么都管。

words.def: a government that is thought to control people's lives too much

cloze.before: To outsiders, such rules can look like a
cloze.after: state at its most fussy.
cloze.szh: 在外人看来，这些规定像是“保姆式国家”管得最琐碎的样子。

words.zh: 挑剔的、过分讲究的；琐碎的
words.note: a fussy eater（挑食的人）。not fussy：无所谓、不挑。
words.ctx: To outsiders, such rules can look like a nanny state at its most fussy.

ex.en: My son is a very [[fussy]] eater.
ex.zh: 我儿子特别挑食。

ex.en: I'm not [[fussy]] — any restaurant is fine.
ex.zh: 我不挑，哪家餐厅都行。

words.def: too worried about small details; hard to please

cf.diff: picky 口语，多指吃东西、挑选“挑剔”；fussy 也可指挑剔，还可指对小事“大惊小怪、过分讲究”。

ex.en: He's a [[picky]] eater.
ex.zh: 他很挑食。

cloze.before: To outsiders, such rules can look like a nanny state at its most
cloze.szh: 在外人看来，这些规定像是“保姆式国家”管得最琐碎的样子。

words.note: un-（不）+ bothered（被打扰的）。口语也说 I'm not bothered.（我无所谓。）
words.ctx: Many residents are unbothered.

ex.en: She seemed [[unbothered]] by the rain.
ex.zh: 她似乎一点也不在意下雨。

ex.en: He stayed calm and [[unbothered]].
ex.zh: 他保持冷静，毫不在意。

words.def: not worried or annoyed by something

cloze.before: Many residents are
cloze.szh: 很多居民对此毫不在意。

words.zh: 一尘不染的、非常干净的
words.note: spot（污点）+ -less（没有）。a spotless kitchen / record（干净的厨房 / 清白的记录）。
words.ctx: They point out that the streets are spotless and the trains run smoothly, and that nobody is being asked to sacrifice more than a minor pleasure.

ex.en: The hotel room was [[spotless]].
ex.zh: 酒店房间一尘不染。

ex.en: He has a [[spotless]] driving record.
ex.zh: 他的驾驶记录毫无污点。

words.def: perfectly clean

cf.diff: clean 是普通的“干净”；spotless 语气强得多，是“一点污渍都没有、一尘不染”。

cloze.before: They point out that the streets are
cloze.after: and the trains run smoothly, and that nobody is being asked to sacrifice more than a minor pleasure.
cloze.szh: 他们指出，街道一尘不染，地铁运行顺畅，而且没有人需要牺牲的不过是一点小小的乐趣。

words.zh: 持续的、顽固的；坚持不懈的
words.note: a persistent cough（久咳不愈），a persistent salesman（死缠烂打的推销员）。名词 persistence。
words.ctx: A persistent myth holds that chewing gum in Singapore can get you caned.

ex.en: I've had a [[persistent]] cough for weeks.
ex.zh: 我咳嗽了好几周都不好。

ex.en: Her [[persistent]] questions finally got an answer.
ex.zh: 她不停追问，终于得到了答复。

words.def: continuing for a long time, often in an annoying way; refusing to give up

cf.diff: persistent 是“持续不断、坚持”（常指让人烦的东西一直不走）；consistent 是“始终如一、前后一致”，多为褒义。

ex.en: Her work is very [[consistent]].
ex.zh: 她的工作水平一直很稳定。

cloze.before: A
cloze.after: myth holds that chewing gum in Singapore can get you caned.
cloze.szh: 有一个流传不衰的说法：在新加坡嚼口香糖会被鞭刑。

words.note: It's a myth that ...：……是个误区。Greek myths（希腊神话）。
words.ctx: A persistent myth holds that chewing gum in Singapore can get you caned.

ex.en: It's a [[myth]] that goldfish forget everything in seconds.
ex.zh: 金鱼几秒钟就忘事，这是个误区。

ex.en: She loves reading Greek [[myths]].
ex.zh: 她爱读希腊神话。

words.def: an ancient story; an idea that many people believe but that is not true

cloze.before: A persistent
cloze.after: holds that chewing gum in Singapore can get you caned.
cloze.szh: 有一个流传不衰的说法：在新加坡嚼口香糖会被鞭刑。

words.note: 动词 cane 指用藤条抽打，作为惩罚；名词 caning（鞭刑、藤条体罚），文中下一句的 the famous caning 就是它。get caned 被打藤条。
words.ctx: A persistent myth holds that chewing gum in Singapore can get you caned.

ex.en: In the past, pupils could be [[caned]] for being rude to a teacher.
ex.zh: 过去，学生对老师无礼可能会挨藤条。

ex.en: He was sentenced to be [[caned]] for the crime.
ex.zh: 他因这项罪行被判鞭刑。

words.def: to hit someone with a long, thin stick as a punishment

cf.diff: 名词 cane 最常见的意思是老人走路用的“手杖”，也指甘蔗、竹子的茎（sugar cane 甘蔗）；动词 cane 才是“用藤条打”。

ex.en: My grandfather walks with a [[cane]].
ex.zh: 我爷爷拄着手杖走路。

cf.diff: beat 是一般的“打、殴打”，可以用手或任何东西；cane 专指用藤条打，而且是作为惩罚。

cloze.before: A persistent myth holds that chewing gum in Singapore can get you
cloze.szh: 有一个流传不衰的说法：在新加坡嚼口香糖会被鞭刑。

words.zh: 故意破坏（公物、他人财物）
words.note: 英式拼写 vandalise，美式 vandalize。做这种事的人是 vandal，这种行为叫 vandalism。常用被动：be vandalised。
words.ctx: It cannot; the famous caning of an American teenager in 1994 was for vandalising cars, not for gum.

ex.en: Someone has [[vandalised]] the phone box again.
ex.zh: 又有人把电话亭搞坏了。

ex.en: The boys were caught [[vandalising]] a school bus.
ex.zh: 那几个男孩在破坏校车时被抓了个正着。

words.def: to deliberately damage things, especially public property (British spelling; American: vandalize)

cf.diff: damage 是一般的“损坏”，可以是意外（The storm damaged the roof.）；vandalise 一定是故意的、无缘无故地破坏，多指公物。

ex.en: The storm [[damaged]] the roof.
ex.zh: 暴风雨把屋顶损坏了。

cloze.before: It cannot; the famous caning of an American teenager in 1994 was for
cloze.after: cars, not for gum.
cloze.szh: 并不会；1994 年那起著名的美国少年被鞭刑事件，是因为他破坏汽车，而不是因为口香糖。

words.note: for my part（就我而言），for their part（就他们而言）。用来引出某一方的态度。
words.ctx: Singaporeans, for their part, tend to treat the ban with amused indifference.

ex.en: [[For my part]], I'm happy to wait.
ex.zh: 就我而言，我很乐意等。

ex.en: The company, [[for its part]], denies everything.
ex.zh: 公司方面则否认一切。

words.def: used to give your own opinion, as different from others'

cloze.before: Singaporeans, for their
cloze.after: , tend to treat the ban with amused indifference.
cloze.szh: 就新加坡人自己而言，他们对这条禁令往往是带着几分好笑的漠不关心。

words.note: 形容词 indifferent（漠不关心的）。with indifference：冷淡地。
words.ctx: Singaporeans, for their part, tend to treat the ban with amused indifference.

ex.en: He listened with complete [[indifference]].
ex.zh: 他听着，完全无动于衷。

ex.en: She was [[indifferent]] to the news.
ex.zh: 她对这个消息漠不关心。

words.def: a lack of interest or concern

cf.diff: indifference 是“漠不关心”；concern / interest 是“关心、在意”。形容词 indifferent to sth 对……无所谓。

ex.en: He is [[indifferent]] to fashion.
ex.zh: 他对时尚毫无兴趣。

cloze.before: Singaporeans, for their part, tend to treat the ban with amused
cloze.szh: 就新加坡人自己而言，他们对这条禁令往往是带着几分好笑的漠不关心。

words.note: 也说 get out of the habit of doing。反义 get into the habit（养成习惯）。
words.ctx: Others say they have simply lost the habit.

ex.en: I've [[lost the habit]] of reading before bed.
ex.zh: 我已经不再睡前看书了。

ex.en: Try not to [[get out of the habit]] of exercising.
ex.zh: 尽量别丢了锻炼的习惯。

words.def: to stop doing something you used to do regularly

cloze.before: Others say they have simply lost the
cloze.szh: 也有人说，他们干脆已经没这个习惯了。

words.zh: 不管怎样（两种情况都一样）；无论哪种
words.note: 前面先说了两种情况，用 either way 表示“不管是哪一种，结果都一样”。文中前两句说有人出国买口香糖、有人已经不想嚼了，either way 引出“口香糖都没回来”。常放句首，后面加逗号。
words.ctx: Either way, the gum has not come back, and neither has the mess.

ex.en: We can take the bus or walk — [[either way]], we'll be late.
ex.zh: 坐公交也好，走路也好，反正我们都会迟到。

ex.en: I don't know if he forgot or just didn't care. [[Either way]], he didn't call.
ex.zh: 我不知道他是忘了还是根本不在乎，总之他没打电话。

words.def: used to say that the result is the same whichever of two things happens or is true

cf.diff: either way 前面要先摆出两种情况，再说“哪种都一样”；anyway 不需要前面有两种情况，只是“不管怎样、总之”，或用来换话题，用得更随意。

ex.en: It was raining, but we went out [[anyway]].
ex.zh: 下着雨，但我们还是出去了。

cf.diff: 意思和 either way 一样，但更正式，多用于书面。

cloze.after: , the gum has not come back, and neither has the mess.
cloze.szh: 不管怎样，口香糖没有回来，那些脏乱也没有回来。

words.note: chew on a pencil（咬铅笔）。比喻：Let me chew on it for a day.（让我琢磨一天。）
words.ctx: In Singapore, at least, some problems stay solved because nobody is allowed to chew on them.

ex.en: The dog likes to [[chew on]] my shoes.
ex.zh: 那只狗喜欢啃我的鞋。

ex.en: Give me a day to [[chew on]] your offer.
ex.zh: 给我一天时间琢磨你的提议。

words.def: to bite food many times; to think carefully about something for a period of time

cloze.before: In Singapore, at least, some problems stay solved because nobody is allowed to
cloze.after: on them.
cloze.szh: 至少在新加坡，有些问题一直不再出现，因为谁也不准再“嚼”它们。
